summary: The Cursed Lands, the grey downs of the Veiled: an Orran people under a council of cord-mothers, the barrows and the knotted cords, sour ground, strangers at the edge and the night the dead walk.

the_veil_spirit.name: The Veil
the_veil_spirit.desc: A veil of stone, custom and something no traveller could name.

the_veil_2.name: A People Apart
the_veil_2.desc: The veil is drawn tighter, and nothing else is anyone's business.

edge_watchers.name: Watchers at the Edge
edge_watchers.desc: Hooded watchers at the border stone, in the same places as their grandmothers.

barrow_lanterns.name: Lanterns on the Mounds
barrow_lanterns.desc: Lit at dusk, burning until dawn, every night since before any record.

barrow_lanterns_2.name: The Mounds Are Quiet
barrow_lanterns_2.desc: The keepers have pronounced the mounds quiet, and the downs hold their breath.

terraces.name: Beds in the Sour Ground
terraces.desc: Roots and mushrooms in walled beds on the sour downs, and nothing wasted.

self_sufficient.name: Enough for Ourselves
self_sufficient.desc: The downs feed, clothe and arm the Veiled, who buy little but salt and iron.

crack_in_the_veil.name: A Crack in the Veil
crack_in_the_veil.desc: A few strangers admitted, a few of the Veiled sent out.

the_dead_walk.name: When the Dead Walk
the_dead_walk.desc: The lanterns on the mounds gutter and flare.

the_old_tallies.title: The Old Tallies
the_old_tallies.desc: The Mother of the Eldest Cord counts what the mounds keep, as every year, on knotted cords in the lantern-light. She does not say what the cords add up to, and no one on the downs has ever thought to ask her.

veiled_envoys.title: Veiled Envoys
veiled_envoys.desc: Hooded envoys of the Cursed Lands have come to the moot of the Red Woods with fruit and a few plain words. They ask only that the forest and the valley leave each other be, and they wait to hear the answer.

tax_men_at_the_edge.title: Tax-Men at the Edge
tax_men_at_the_edge.desc: A party of Parim's tax-men has reached the border stone, courteous, persistent and entirely lost. The watchers could turn them back, or they could pay a small token to be left in peace.

a_scholar_asks.title: A Scholar Asks
a_scholar_asks.desc: A scholar of the Lost Cause stands at the border stone and asks, very politely, to read the tallies of the barrows. The cord-mothers are told, and the watchers wait for a nod, a pause or an empty chair.

almoners_at_the_edge.title: Almoners at the Edge
almoners_at_the_edge.desc: Almoners of the Deliverer wait at the border stone with bread, linen and a plan for a hospital on the downs. The watchers send word to the cord-mothers, who are patient, and so are they.

focuses.name: The Veil
focuses.desc: The Cursed Lands lie behind a veil that is partly stone, partly custom and partly something no traveller has ever been able to name. Parim calls the land cursed; its people do not say why.

focuses.name: No Road In
focuses.desc: The roads into the downs are closed with stone and thorn, and the passes are narrowed to a footpath. Anyone who wishes to enter must first be seen to have a reason.

focuses.name: The Mothers' Silence
focuses.desc: The council of cord-mothers governs the downs and says very little. A decision of the council is a nod, a pause or an empty chair, and the Veiled have always understood which is which.

focuses.name: Watchers at the Edge
focuses.desc: Hooded watchers stand at the edge of the downs, in the same places their grandmothers stood. They wave no one in, and they wave no one off.

focuses.name: The Unspoken Law
focuses.desc: There is a law on the downs that is never written and never spoken, and no one has ever been found who broke it twice.

focuses.name: A People Apart
focuses.desc: The Veiled agree that they are a people apart, and the veil is drawn tighter. They want to be left alone, and nothing else about them is anyone's business.

focuses.name: The Veil Holds
focuses.desc: The veil has held for longer than the Concord has stood. It will go on holding, so long as no one looks too closely at what it is made of.

focuses.name: The Barrow-Keepers
focuses.desc: The downs keep barrows older than the Concord, and a line of keepers older than the barrows. They speak of them as the mounds, and of what the mounds keep as nothing in particular.

focuses.name: Lanterns on the Mounds
focuses.desc: Lanterns are lit on the mounds at dusk and kept burning until dawn. They have been lit every night since before any record, and the tallow is never allowed to run low.

focuses.name: The Old Tallies
focuses.desc: The Mother of the Eldest Cord counts what the mounds keep, as every year. The count is tied into the cords, and nobody outside the downs has ever seen one.

focuses.name: Quiet Earth
focuses.desc: The earth over the mounds is kept still: no plough, no spade, no wandering goat. The keepers say a quiet earth is a quiet sleep.

focuses.name: The Keepers' Oath
focuses.desc: Each keeper swears an oath that is spoken only once, in the dark, at the foot of the oldest mound. What it says is not known beyond the valley, and not all of it within.

focuses.name: The Mounds Are Quiet
focuses.desc: The keepers pronounce the mounds quiet, and a hush falls on the downs. It is a hush of the kind one hears before a storm, or after one.

focuses.name: The Hidden Downs
focuses.desc: The downs are hidden from every road, and the one way in is a goat-track under an overhang. Inside, the ground is grey and sour, and every root and mushroom bed on it is tended as carefully as a child.

focuses.name: Beds in the Sour Ground
focuses.desc: Nothing sown in the usual way will grow on the sour downs, so the Veiled grow roots and mushrooms in deep beds walled with dry stone and mended every spring. Nothing is wasted, and nothing is sold.

focuses.name: Charcoal and Iron
focuses.desc: Charcoal-burners and smelters work in a hidden gully, their smoke drawn away down a long flue so that no stranger will ever see it.

focuses.name: The Inner Smithy
focuses.desc: The smiths of the downs work behind closed doors, and the work that leaves their forge is never marked. Their blades are plain and extremely sharp.

focuses.name: Enough for Ourselves
focuses.desc: The Veiled feed, clothe and arm themselves from the downs, and they trade at the edge only roots and mushrooms for salt and iron. They are well content to keep it that way.

focuses.name: Strangers at the Edge
focuses.desc: Strangers arrive at the edge, usually one at a time, usually hungry. The watchers meet each at the border stone and hear what they have to say.

focuses.name: Words with the Redbarks
focuses.desc: The Redbark of the red woods speak the same old tongue as the Veiled and have never asked to enter. The cord-mothers send a messenger with roots, fruit and a few plain words.

focuses.name: The Tax-Men Turned Back
focuses.desc: Parim's tax-men have reached the edge of the downs with their ledgers and their escorts. They are courteous, they are persistent, and they have not understood where they are.

focuses.name: A Scholar at the Edge
focuses.desc: A scholar of the Lost Cause has walked a long way to ask a question. The watchers hear it and send word to the cord-mothers, who do not answer.

focuses.name: Healers from Outside
focuses.desc: Almoners of the Deliverer come to the edge with bread and medicine and a plan for a hospital. The watchers send them back to the border stone and tell them to wait.

focuses.name: A Crack in the Veil
focuses.desc: A few strangers are admitted to the downs, and a few of the Veiled are sent out in return. The veil is not lifted, only thinned, and the cord-mothers say nothing at all.

focuses.name: When the Dead Walk
focuses.desc: The lanterns on the mounds gutter and flare. Whatever the barrows keep, the dead have begun to walk elsewhere, and the downs must choose what they will do about it.

focuses.name: Bar the Barrows
focuses.desc: Every barrow is sealed with stone and thorn, and the keepers take their stations on the mounds. The veil is drawn tight, and what the mounds keep will keep.

focuses.name: Open the Veil
focuses.desc: The cord-mothers lift the veil. The Veiled go out among the living with their bows and their silence, and the living find that they are very good company in a dark hour.

focuses.name: The Long Night Watch
focuses.desc: The watchers are doubled and then doubled again. They stand through the long nights with lanterns and bows, and they do not talk about what they are watching for.

focuses.name: With the Living
focuses.desc: The Veiled come out in their grey hoods to stand with the Heir. They ask for nothing, and they say very little, and they fight as if they had been waiting for this all their lives.

focuses.name: The Veil Mended
focuses.desc: The war is over, and the cord-mothers draw the veil closed once more. Whatever came out has gone back in, and the lanterns on the mounds burn steady again.

focuses.name: What the Cords Count
focuses.desc: The eldest cord-mother lays the cords of every line side by side, which has not been done in living memory. The ties run back past the Withdrawal and on into years for which the downs keep no other name, and far more of them are black than anyone expected.

focuses.name: The Last Cord Shown
focuses.desc: The cord-mothers bring the Last Cord up out of the eldest barrow and let the other Orran houses see it. Whoever wants to know where it lies will now find out, and the mothers have decided that the Redbark should know first.

focuses.name: The Last Cord Hidden
focuses.desc: The mothers move the Last Cord out of the eldest barrow by night, and only three of them know where it went. A stranger who takes the barrow will find stones and silence there and nothing else.

focuses.name: Words with the Stone-Counters
focuses.desc: A cord-mother walks west to the giants of the ring with a cord in her satchel. The cairn-keepers are said to count the same years in stone, and the mothers would like to know whether the two counts agree.

focuses.name: Words with the Tide-Queens
focuses.desc: The queens of the isle houses choose their queen at the turn of the tide and give their dead to the sea, much as the mothers did long ago. A grey-hooded envoy takes ship for Borrak to ask what else the tide remembers.

focuses.name: The Moot of Mothers
focuses.desc: The cords and the stones agree, and the mothers now know what their grandmothers would never say aloud. They talk of a moot that sat before any crown, and of what it would mean to sit in it again.
